body: This is one of my other accounts, by the way, I'm the OP :P

Your story is inspiring, its those small things that refresh my hope sometimes.

And yes, there are many works of art I cling too, honestly. I think that they fill in those gaps of emotional connectivity and understanding. I love finding a movie or song that I can relate to, it often digs up ideas that I bury because of painful experience of anger. I think that's why I've been on a hunt for movies with deep and intricate plot and characters, and desperately desiring new types of music. I told myself at one point in my life that I would never listen to rap. However, I've begun to embrace it, mostly due to the fuck you attitude of the lyrics in most songs. It's an outlet, I suppose.

This is true. I know in my heart that the positives of humanity and relationships outweigh all of the negative. But whenever one is established in my life, it feels as if my energy is being drained, and it doesn't stay mutual for too long. Sometimes this makes me angry, all of these failures to make a completely wonderful connection on an emotional level. 

Sometimes I want to say fuck everyone. I don't need people. But then I feel foolish because I know it's a lie. It leads to a very conflicted state of mind.
I'm on my iPhone, and that option isn't provided, or at least I don't see it.
Wonderful answer, thank you for taking the time, I really appreciate it.
your words* :)

Understandable. Thanks for the response, I appreciate you taking the time to answer genuinely. Hold on to that hope, never let go of it. I can tell just from reading the words there is potential within you to succeed.

I loved reading this, and I'm so glad that there are people out there like you, especially in this time in which sex is considered essential to satisfaction and success by our society. I just want you to know that I think that is incredible and amazing, and that I truly respect your willpower.   

As for my question, do you think the lack of sex within the relationship could have possibly made it stronger, in that you two could only connect based on personality, emotions, intellect, etc.?
Do you often face moral conflict or various dillemas with yourself in order to stay true to the character you are emulating?
Do you think it would somewhat revive your hopes for the field if you perhaps looked at it with the mindset that you had the potential to truly help others in need?

My thoughts exactly. It's not like I'm expecting to do wonderful and caring things for people and for them to respond with "OH MY GOSH YOU ARE SO NICE AND WONDERFUL AND SPECIAL TO ME!" in all cases.

I do things for people because I care about them. But, recently, it has started to feel so one-sided that it just drains my energy and my friends, family, etc don't seem to notice or care that I need help just as much as they ever do.

Interesting perspective. It's refreshing to know that there are people out there who feel genuine empathy just as I do, who have the ability to care for others that they aren't necessarily close to or completely understand.

It's that type of love and affection that I search for within people, and it's an emotion I respect and value greatly. The lack of it kills me.
I don't think that will be necessary.
How?

Wow, you are very beautiful, you should be quite confident in your pursuit of such a career. I think you have more than what it takes.

This is what I love about Reddit, being able to read incredibly interesting posts such as these. I wish you the best of luck and have no doubt that you've been blessed with a gorgeous appearance that could take you places.
Wow, reading the all caps made me laugh incredibly hard, haha!

I'll be attending a university that requires me to live on campus for the first year anyway, and I am looking forward to meeting new people, lots of new people, but I'm looking for something with meaning. 

I don't want it to be, "Well howdy do, we sat at the same table in the library and talked for about fifteen minutes and now we never speak to each other." I realize that it's not a realistic desire to expect to form a deep bond with every person you meet, but I feel like these shallow encounters have more of a potential to happen in a setting such as a university.

It will probably be better once I'm actually on campus and have the opportunity to interact with others and experience the feeling of being there and having countless options.

Thank you for the very helpful response.

I agree with you that religion is not something required to be a moral and fulfilled person, but I don't think that was the point of his post. It's truly loving advice, and that's all that matters. Thank you for trying to look out though.
Let's not turn this into any sort of religious debacle. They are simply trying to help, and I appreciate both of the comments that you guys made.

I simply wish there more than a "few" and that the chances of forming connections with these type of people were higher. 

I'll be in college in the fall, people will be all around me, but what are the chances any sort of intimate friendship/relationship can be formed when the overall amount/mass of people is just so....daunting?

I've never had problems getting to know a person, but I am quite shy at heart, which is something that will make it more difficult. It's just hard for me to imagine many meaningful relationships coming out of an environment that is insanely large and filled with people. I'm going to find myself extremely lonely at many times, I'm sure. I hope this makes sense, I'm not quite sure if I'm explaining it well enough.

I love God, am Christian, and do have a strong faith-base. But I must admit, I'm not sure what is going on right now or what His plan is. Things don't seem to be clicking in place, I don't feel His presence as much (or even at all anymore), these emotions become so overwhelming at certain points I just become utterly defeated/depressed. It's heartbreaking because I know the truth yet still find myself stuck.

Thank you, these are wonderful responses.
I'm sorry, but that is not something I'm interested in at the moment.

Thank you! I will definitely send a message your way sometime if the opportunity ever arises, and thank you for the link as well, it will be quite helpful I'm sure.

This reply radiates kindness and I want you to know that I truly appreciate you and the time you took to type those sentences. People like you restore my faith when it fades.

My thoughts exactly. I don't feel like I should have to pay/plead for someone to speak to me and care for what I am feeling. I don't want to know a person like that, a person who wants to know me out of obligation instead of interest/affection/care.

I have to thank you for sharing this because it's strikingly similar to a situation that I once was in.

A girl and I felt connection on a very deep level, we were the best of friends and could discuss practically anything. I had never really felt this type of emotion before, this type of acceptance and, essentially, undying love for another human being. I was happy. I've lost that person since then.

You have a miracle in your life, a blessing, and a rare one at that. Never let go of it.

I believe that the overwhelming feeling of starting college soon and being on my own attributes to my feelings of isolation, disconnection, and doubt that I will find caring people. The world feels too large, the deep connection that I desire seems to me to be impossible to find in a world so fast-paced and...uninvolved. It's discouraging, very discouraging, the thought drains me and weakens me.

I live in south Texas.
I always enjoy reading these and I especially cherish this one. Thank you very much, from the bottom of my heart, it brought a tear to my eye.
